identifierPolicy: urn:tsmm:concept:<slug> identifiers are stable semantic references. Renaming a label does not change the identifier; withdrawal or supersession must be explicit.

concepts.label: GovernanceAuthority
concepts.definition: Authority to define, constrain, delegate, or revoke governance-relevant action.

concepts.label: Delegation
concepts.definition: A bounded transfer or attenuation of authority from an originating authority to a delegate.

concepts.label: Scope
concepts.definition: The explicit boundary within which authority, evidence, policy, or a decision is applicable.

concepts.label: Policy
concepts.definition: A rule or rule-set evaluated when determining whether a requested effect may be admitted.

concepts.label: EvidenceArtifact
concepts.definition: An inspectable artifact offered in support of a governance, assurance, or trust claim.

concepts.label: EvidenceBundle
concepts.definition: A governed collection of evidence artifacts assembled for evaluation or audit.

concepts.label: Assessment
concepts.definition: An evaluation of evidence, controls, policy, or state against declared criteria.

concepts.label: TrustDecision
concepts.definition: A bounded decision produced from authority, policy, evidence, and evaluation context.

concepts.label: Effect
concepts.definition: An operational consequence admitted, denied, constrained, or recorded by a trust decision.

concepts.label: TrustRegistry
concepts.definition: A governed publication or discovery surface for trust-relevant state.

concepts.label: AssuranceProfile
concepts.definition: A declared set of assurance expectations, rigor, evidence, or control requirements.

concepts.label: Revocation
concepts.definition: The invalidation or withdrawal of previously usable authority, state, evidence, or permission.

concepts.label: Supersession
concepts.definition: An explicit lifecycle event by which a newer authoritative artifact replaces an earlier artifact.

concepts.label: Redress
concepts.definition: A governed path for contesting, reviewing, correcting, or remedying a trust-system outcome.

concepts.label: DecisionTransitionBasis
concepts.definition: The inspectable semantic category identifying which material input change caused a trust decision to transition, without implying that authority changed.

concepts.label: MaterialUnresolvedCondition
concepts.definition: A material proposition relevant to a trust decision or effect that remains unresolved until an admissible authority, evidence, policy, lifecycle, proposition, or correction event changes its basis.
